thread.title: Enemy Performance Optimization
thread.preview:
Yep, the screenshots exposed the actual problem: **the top HP bar was correct; the CHARACTER panel was adding equipment bonuses twice.**

For example:

- Real maximum HP: **435**
- Equipped flat HP shown: **+136**
- Incorrect CHARACTER value: **435 + 136 = 571**

The same happened with speed:

- Real calculated speed: **210**
- Equipped flat speed: **+60**
- Incorrect displayed speed: **270**

That likely made the first respawn feel as though your speed had disappeared, while the second respawn’s temporary `1.35×` reconstruction boost made it feel closer to the false displayed value.

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}[Download the 0.25.6b Reconstruction Stat-Sync Patch](sandbox:/mnt/data/syntethic-ascension-0.0.0.25.6b-reconstruction-stat-sync-patch.zip)

Apply it **after 0.25.6a**.

### Fixed

- CHARACTER HP now matches the top HP bar.
- All CHARACTER totals no longer add inventory stats twice.
- Movement and displayed SPD now use the same authoritative calculation.
- Temporary Conduit and reconstruction speed multipliers appear in the displayed SPD.
- First respawn rebuilds race, style, equipment, augments, sets and item-effect stats before restoring HP.
- Respawn restores HP using the final recalculated maximum.
- Old movement velocity is cleared during reconstruction.
- HP values now use consistent rounding in both displays.

The patch passed archive integrity, checksum, patch-reapplication and targeted static checks. Godot runtime testing still needs confirming, particularly:

1. Speed immediately after the **first** death.
2. Speed after the **second** death.
3. Top HP and CHARACTER HP matching before and after respawning.

Done — **patch-only ZIP** for the two bugs:

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}[Download 0.25.6a Respawn + Splitter Bugfix Patch](sandbox:/mnt/data/syntethic-ascension-0.0.0.25.6a-respawn-splitter-bugfix-patch.zip)

### Fixed

**Relay completion after death**

The relay continued attuning because the dead player remained at the death position while the reconstruction window was open. Relay activation and progress now pause while `is_dead` is true. Legitimately completed relay nodes remain completed.

**Splitter item multiplication**

A complete Splitter family now receives only **one original item roll**:

- The original Splitter rolls its normal drop chance once.
- On success, one immediate child inherits the guaranteed item.
- Other children and descendants cannot independently roll items.
- When no child can spawn, the original drops the item instead.
- Health pickups and follower rewards remain per enemy body.

The archive passed checksum, path, reapplication, ZIP-integrity and targeted static-logic checks. Godot is unavailable here, so editor parsing and gameplay still need testing.

Once both fixes behave correctly, the next build needed for the lightweight Grunt/Runner prototype is the full project with this 0.25.6a patch applied.

items.text:
I only need the **full current game ZIP with the 0.25.6 performance patch already applied**.

From that build I’ll first fix:

1. **Respawn quest-state bug**  
   Dying and respawning must restore the segment to its actual unfinished state. The end gate must remain locked until the first objective is genuinely completed.

2. **Splitter duplicate drops**  
   The small split enemies must not each independently roll the original enemy’s loot. When the original Splitter was eligible to drop an item, **only one descendant inherits that drop**, so the whole Splitter family produces at most the intended single item.

Then the next performance stage would be the **lightweight enemy prototype**:

- Convert only Grunts and Runners initially.
- Manager-owned positions, health, cooldowns and states.
- Batched rendering.
- Grid/flow-field collision instead of `CharacterBody2D`.
- Compatibility with bullets, melee, AoE, status effects, drops and contact damage.
- Keep all complex enemies as normal Nodes.
- Add a debug toggle so the lightweight version can be compared directly against the old enemies.

No screenshots or extra explanation are necessary unless either bug behaves differently from what you described. Just send the current full ZIP.

content.text:
How would it be possible to upgrade FPS, okay, in one of the old patches all bullets were actual objects, but it got changed, so it's just sprites(?), so is something similar possible with enemies?

Domāja 3m 5s

Yes, something similar is possible with enemies, but enemies are much harder than bullets.

The bullets are not merely individual sprites now. ProjectileSimulationManager.gd stores them as rows of data in packed arrays:

Position
Velocity
Damage
Lifetime
Radius
Team
Visual type

One manager updates all bullets in one loop, and one MultiMeshInstance2D renders them. Ordinary bullets have no separate Node, Area2D, timer or _physics_process().

Enemies are still much heavier. Every normal enemy currently has:

CharacterBody2D
Sprite2D
Physical collision shape
Separate hitbox Area2D
Its own _physics_process()
move_and_slide()
Navigation, separation and stuck detection
Several AI-module ticks
Health, effects and drop handling
EnemyIndex updates

At 180 ambient enemies, that can mean 10,800 enemy physics ticks and move_and_slide() calls each second, before summons, split enemies, boss adds and interiors.

Full data-oriented enemies

The equivalent of the bullet rewrite would be an EnemySwarmManager.

Ordinary enemies would become data:

PackedVector2Array positions
PackedVector2Array velocities
PackedFloat32Array health
PackedFloat32Array attack_cooldowns
PackedInt32Array enemy_types
PackedInt32Array states
PackedInt64Array enemy_ids

The manager would:

Move all basic enemies in one loop.
Sample the existing shared flow field.
Perform simple separation through spatial buckets.
Handle health and status effects.
Detect contact with the player.
Process deaths and drops.
Render enemies through MultiMeshInstance2D.
Remove enemies through swap-removal, like the projectile manager.

There would be no separate Sprite, CharacterBody, hitbox or script instance for each basic enemy.

What should remain normal Nodes

I would not convert every enemy.

Keep these as the existing EnemyActor scenes:

Bosses and minibosses
Elites
Snipers
Summoners
Heralds
Chargers
Bombers
Objective enemies
Enemies with unusual attacks or complicated states

First migrate only high-volume fodder:

Grunt
Runner
Summoned Minion
Basic Splitter offspring
Possibly basic Leech enemies later

That gives most of the performance benefit without rewriting every enemy mechanic.

Why simply changing Sprite2D to MultiMesh would not be enough

Enemy rendering is only part of the cost. Godot may already batch some ordinary canvas sprites.

The larger enemy costs are probably:

CharacterBody2D.move_and_slide() for every enemy every frame.
One physics body and one hitbox area per enemy.
Per-enemy _physics_process().
Wall sliding and collision resolution.
AI-module updates.
Separation and navigation sampling.
Status-effect Nodes and timers.
Group scans that remain in a few spells and enemy modules.

So replacing 180 Sprite2Ds with one MultiMesh while leaving 180 CharacterBodies underneath would provide only part of the gain.

The real upgrade is:

Data simulation + batched rendering + centralised collision queries.

Your projectile system already makes this easier

ProjectileSimulationManager does not need enemy hitbox signals for ordinary bullets. It queries EnemyIndex, checks each enemy as a circle and sends damage directly.

That means normal bullets are already close to being compatible with data enemies.

The larger conversion work would be:

Melee currently detects enemy_hitbox areas.
Some magic attacks scan enemy Nodes or hitboxes.
Player contact damage depends on enemy hitbox overlap.
Several augments call take_damage() on enemy Nodes.
Status effects currently expect an enemy Node target.

Those systems would need one shared enemy-target interface capable of addressing either:

A normal EnemyActor Node, or
A lightweight manager-owned enemy handle.

For example:

EnemyTargetRef:
    kind: NODE or SWARM
    node: Node
    enemy_id: int

Spells should query the central enemy registry and apply damage through that interface instead of assuming every target is a Node.

Collision in the generated city

This is the difficult part.

Data enemies cannot simply do:

position += velocity * delta

or they will walk through buildings.

Fortunately, the project already has:

FlowFieldNav
Chunk walkability data
World-blocker geometry
A spatial enemy index

Basic swarm enemies could use grid-based collision:

Sample flow direction.
Propose the next position.
Check whether the corresponding navigation cells are walkable.
Try horizontal and vertical sliding when blocked.
Keep the previous position when neither direction works.

That would be cheaper than hundreds of move_and_slide() calls, but it needs careful testing in two-cell alleys, doorways and courtyard passages.

A safer intermediate optimisation

Before rewriting enemies completely, I would add simulation LOD.

Near enemies

Within approximately 1,000–1,200 pixels:

Full physics
Full AI
Full hitbox
Normal attack timing
Normal separation
Medium-distance enemies

Approximately 1,200–2,500 pixels:

AI decision update at 10–15 Hz
No LOS raycast unless required
Separation update less often
Expensive modules update only when their cooldown is near completion
Visual motion interpolated between updates
Far enemies

Beyond approximately 2,500 pixels:

Flow-field movement at 3–5 Hz
No separation
No ordinary hitbox monitoring
No attacks
No wall-assist logic
Despawn quickly when outside loaded/relevant chunks

This would preserve the current enemy architecture while considerably reducing unnecessary work.

Smaller current-code improvements

Even without the major rewrite, there are several obvious optimisations:

Cache the EnemyIndex reference instead of calling get_node_or_null("/root/EnemyIndex") from every enemy every frame.
Lower max_slides from 8 to approximately 3–4 for basic enemies.
Tick only the AI modules that the enemy type actually uses.
Update flow direction and separation on staggered intervals.
Replace remaining get_nodes_in_group("enemies") scans in Wardstone, Herald, Tactical and several spells with EnemyIndex queries.
Maintain ambient and special counts incrementally instead of repeatedly looping over all registered enemies.
Disable dormant interior enemy processing completely.
Pool ordinary enemy Nodes, deaths and hit effects even before converting enemies to data.
Cull trapped ambient enemies that have made no meaningful progress for 10–12 seconds.
Recommended development order
Performance patch 1 — low risk
Harder culling
Stuck-enemy cleanup
Cached manager references
Remove remaining group scans
AI update staggering
Near/mid/far processing tiers
Disable distant hitbox monitoring
Performance overlay showing enemy physics and AI cost
Performance patch 2 — lightweight swarm prototype

Convert only EnemyGrunt and EnemyRunner into:

Packed-array simulation
MultiMesh rendering
Grid collision
Manager-owned health
Central contact damage
Existing projectile-manager compatibility

Then stress-test:

50 enemies
100 enemies
180 enemies
300 lightweight enemies
Performance patch 3 — combat-system integration

Adapt:

Melee
Magic AoE
Augments
Burn and bleed
Knockback and stun
Drops and lifesteal

Then migrate summoned minions and basic split offspring.

So, yes, enemies can receive the bullet treatment. The best architecture is a hybrid: hundreds of ordinary swarm enemies as manager-owned data, while distinctive enemies remain full Nodes. That is probably the largest possible enemy-side FPS improvement, but the tiered-processing patch should come first because it is much safer and will reveal how much of the full rewrite is actually necessary.

[User attached 1 file; file contents were not included]

items.text:
Done — this is a **patch-only ZIP** for 0.25.5:

:chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}[Download the 0.25.6 Enemy Performance Patch](sandbox:/mnt/data/syntethic-ascension-0.0.0.25.6-enemy-performance-patch.zip)

### Implemented

- Near/mid/far simulation LOD for ordinary Grunts, Runners, Splitters and Leeches.
- Mid enemies recalculate steering at roughly 12.5 Hz.
- Far enemies recalculate at 5 Hz, skip separation and disable their regular hitbox until closer.
- Movement remains physics-rate, so enemies should not visibly teleport.
- Bosses, elites, objective enemies and complex archetypes retain full processing.
- Ordinary swarm enemies use four physics slides instead of eight.
- Enemies now tick only their relevant AI modules.
- Cached `EnemyIndex`, player, chunk-manager and hitbox references.
- O(1) enemy population and per-type counts.
- Deaths immediately release spawn and summon capacity.
- Wardstone pulses now query nearby enemies through `EnemyIndex`.
- Projectile manager no longer searches the scene tree every physics frame.

This **does not yet convert enemies into packed-array/MultiMesh entities**. It is the safer first performance stage before attempting a Grunt/Runner swarm manager.

The archive was applied successfully to a fresh copy of 0.25.5, its internal checksums passed, and all six scripts passed static structure checks. I could not launch Godot in this environment, so actual parsing, gameplay behavior and FPS improvement still need testing inside the project.
